question.problem:
Find, **in radians**, the argument of $z=-4+6\text{i}.$ Round your final answer to **two decimal places**.

**Hint**: The argument of a complex number is in the range $[0,2\pi ).$ 

$\operatorname{arg}⁡(z)≈$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Let's plot $z$ in the complex plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226152/assets/325444dbc509efd27f6c5bf16c751b137532e2566a9dfaa69f92d9ce16bac51b.png)

The complex number $z$ lies in the second quadrant of the complex plane. Hence $\frac{\pi }{2}<\operatorname{arg}⁡(z)<\pi .$ 

If $\alpha $ is the angle that $z$ makes with the negative real axis, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡\alpha  & =\frac{6}{4} \\ \alpha  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{6}{4}) \\  & =0.982\text{ }793…\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z)=\pi -0.982\text{ }793…≈2.16,
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
